entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_entire-prod-us__resolve_entire_repo
entries.description:
Resolve a repository reference to its canonical, region-local storage ULID (and a console link).

When to use:
  - FIRST call whenever you only have a repo name, path, or URL — the canonical entry point.
  - Any tool rejected a ULID as belonging to another region — re-resolve here and continue with the returned repo_id.

Repo ULIDs are region-scoped: the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never hand-carry a ULID across regions or sessions — pass a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) and use the repo_id this returns.

Pairs with: every repo-scoped tool (they accept the returned repo_id or the original path); list_entire_repos (browse when the name is unknown).

Examples:
  - Resolve a GitHub-surfaced repo: repo="gh/entirehq/mirror-pipeline"

repo.description: the repository: a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, or git/<owner>/<repo>) or a 26-char repo ULID

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_entire-prod-us__search_entire_code
entries.description:
Exact code search across indexed repos, in three modes.

When to use:
  - "Which code contains this exact string?" — mode=content (default; case_sensitive optional).
  - "Find files named *handler*" — mode=files (fuzzy path lookup).
  - "Where is symbol X?" — mode=symbols (fuzzy symbol lookup; symbol_kind, definitions_only).

Searches the indexed default-branch head, not arbitrary refs — for a specific ref use get_entire_file / get_entire_tree. Do NOT use for conceptual "where did we discuss X" questions — use search_entire.

Code search is gated per jurisdiction: where the index is not deployed, this reports that clearly.

Pairs with: get_entire_file (open a hit, optionally with symbols); search_entire (semantic complement); resolve_entire_repo (canonicalize repo refs).

mode.description: content (default, exact match), files (fuzzy path lookup), or symbols (fuzzy symbol lookup)

repo.description: restrict to specific repos (prefixed path or ULID); omit to search all indexed repos

case_sensitive.description: only for mode content; default is case-insensitive

symbol_kind.description: only for mode symbols; filter by symbol kind (e.g. function, type)

definitions_only.description: only for mode symbols; return only definitions

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_entire-prod-us__get_entire_tree
entries.description:
List a directory tree at a ref.

When to use:
  - "What's the structure of this repo / directory?" — scope with path.
  - Orienting in an unfamiliar repo before reading files.

recursive=true on a large repo can be huge — prefer a scoped path.

Pairs with: get_entire_file (read what you find).

repo.description: the repository: a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, or git/<owner>/<repo>) or a 26-char repo ULID

ref.description: branch, tag, or SHA whose tree to list

path.description: subdirectory to list; empty lists the root

recursive.description: walk the whole subtree rather than one level

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_entire-prod-us__list_entire_repos
entries.description:
List repositories the caller can read, with repo facts (stars, forks, language, checkpoint/PR counts, activity). Sortable/filterable over those facts; paginate with cursor.

When to use:
  - "What repos do we have / which are active?" — orientation before drilling in.
  - Finding a repo by org, language, or exact name to then resolve_entire_repo and read.

Set scope=all to also surface onboardable GitHub repos not yet in Entire.

Do NOT use to find a repo by topic or fuzzy meaning — use search_entire.

Pairs with: resolve_entire_repo (canonicalize a chosen repo); get_entire_repo_overview (drill into one repo's analytics).

Examples:
  - One org's repos, most active first: org="entirehq", sort="last_activity_at:desc"
  - Name substring lookup: q="mirror-pipeline"

cursor.description: opaque cursor from a prior response's next_cursor

scope.description: onboarded (default): repos already in Entire; all: also include onboardable GitHub candidates

order.description: direction for a single bare sort key: asc (default) or desc

language.description: filter to an exact repo language

has_checkpoints.description: true: repos with checkpoints; false: repos with none

q.description: literal case-insensitive substring match on full_name (owner/repo); not fuzzy

status.description: placement lifecycle: mirrored, processing, or inactive (inactive requires scope=all)

permission.description: minimum caller access: read (all), write, or admin

limit.description: max repos per page (server caps at 200)

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_entire-prod-us__search_entire
entries.description:
Semantic/hybrid search across repos, checkpoints, commits, PRs, and sessions.

When to use:
  - "Where did we discuss X?" / "the session where we fixed the ULID bug" — a vague description to an entity.
  - "Any prior work on Y?" — topic discovery across entity types before starting new work.

Matches by meaning as well as keywords. Returns a single ranked page; raise limit for more.

Do NOT use for exact strings, symbols, or file paths — that is code search (a later tool).

Pairs with: resolve_entire_repo / get_entire_checkpoint / get_entire_session (drill into a returned hit).

Examples:
  - Topic search: query="ULID region resolution bug"
  - Sessions only on one branch: query="flaky trail gate timeout", types=["sessions"], repo=["et/platform/entire-api"], branch="main"

types.description: entity types to search: repos, checkpoints, commits, prs, sessions. Defaults to all

repo.description: restrict to specific repos (prefixed path or ULID)

date.description: restrict to the last week or month; omit for all time

limit.description: max ranked results to return (1-500, default 20)

content.thinking:
I've found that the server half exists in entirehq/entire-api, with commits by Suhaan Thayyil in July-August 2026 across several audit and fix branches related to the brain component.

These branches implement: the brain artifact publish endpoint with validation and encryption over an object store, a FactSetStore with CAS head proven against Postgres, fact-set sync endpoints with 412 CAS semantics, proposal-set endpoints, brain MCP read tools with schema version negotiation, and a hash-chained advance log with encrypted blobs using crypto-shredding.

But there's a key caveat — one note explicitly says "the server wiring that turns it on is #242," meaning these endpoints might exist on branches without being wired into main. Since commits live on `audit/*` branches and the production OpenAPI spec has no `/brain` paths, I need to verify whether these were ever merged or if the feature is simply disabled (which would explain a nil publisher returning 503).

I'm noting that if the endpoints were deployed but just unconfigured, OpenAPI would still list the paths — so the more likely explanation is these commits never made it into main, or were merged but excluded from the public spec. I want to confirm this by checking which branches contain a given commit, or by tracing PR #242 directly. I'm also confirming the store backend is Postgres, and that the crypto-shredding design means the server does envelope encryption server-side — authorized runners get decrypted plaintext back, so this isn't end-to-end encrypted. Now I need to check whether these audit commits actually exist on entire-api's main branch, using branch-containing lookups or by inspecting the PR trail for #242.

I found the server-side work in `entirehq/entire-api`: FactSetStore over Postgres with encrypted blobs, crypto-shredding, CAS/proposal endpoints, and brain MCP tools, built across milestones P1.M1.5–M3.2. Now I'll check whether this is merged to main and why prod doesn't expose it.

I notice main's internal directory lacks brainbuild/brainstore but does include factsoutbox, factsrelay, snapshotstore, snapshotcrypt, secretcrypt, gitmeta, and records — so it seems the P1 brain milestones live on a separate audit branch rather than main.

The brain-related work must be confined to audit/* branches, not merged into main. Meanwhile factsrelay on main resembles the cross-cell relay pattern seen in sessionnamesrelay, settingsrelay, and trailsrelay, so "facts" here might refer to a different entity than brain facts — I should check a factsoutbox file header to clarify what it actually relays.
The brain server work from P1 only exists on unmerged audit/* branches, not on main — but main does have factsoutbox and factsrelay packages, so I'll check if those relate to brain facts.

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_entire-prod-us__get_entire_file
entries.description:
Read one file's content at a ref, optionally with its symbols.

When to use:
  - Open a file at a specific branch, tag, or SHA (ref); omit ref for the default-branch head.
  - Symbols overview of a file — omit ref and set include_symbols (indexed head only; gated).

Large files are truncated to max_tokens with a next_cursor to continue (binary content is returned base64).

Do NOT use to find files — that is search_entire_code.

Pairs with: get_entire_tree (browse directories); compare_entire_refs (see what changed); search_entire_code (find the file).

repo.description: the repository: a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, or git/<owner>/<repo>) or a 26-char repo ULID

ref.description: branch, tag, or SHA to read at; omit for the default-branch head (must be omitted with include_symbols)

include_symbols.description: attach the file's symbols from the code index (only without ref; gated per jurisdiction)

max_tokens.description: token budget (default 10000); large files truncate with a next_cursor to continue

content.thinking:
I realize the factsoutbox/factsrelay naming is just a coincidence — those are repo stats facts for entire-core, unrelated to brain durable facts. So the real conclusion stands: entire-api main has no brain server code at all, since the actual brainstore/brainbuild/httpapi implementation only exists on unmerged audit/* branches.

This shifts the whole design question toward resurrecting or merging those audit branches rather than rebuilding from scratch, especially since commit messages suggest live end-to-end testing against the released brain client was done. I want to check how current and alive those branches still are, so I should list branches matching audit/brain* to see how far behind main they sit — I'll try the repo branches endpoint to pull that list.

The `factsoutbox`/`factsrelay` on main are unrelated — they handle repo stats, not brain memories, so the actual brain server work lives on the `audit/*` branches. I'll check the state of those branches next.

The user is saying no serverside code exists for this path and it needs to be built from scratch, which contradicts what I found earlier about m4-brain-* branches in entire-api. The user describes entire-api as just a reverse proxy routing to internal services, but I have concrete evidence of commits on those branches — so either the user is unaware of recent work, or I'm misreading what those branches actually contain.

I should trust the user's direction to build a new internal service from scratch, while briefly flagging that those existing branches could be a useful reference for design or code, rather than re-arguing the point.

Going through the decisions: the service sits behind entire-api as a reverse proxy, backed by the existing Aurora cluster, reusing existing auth patterns. Scope covers memories at the branch/trail and repo level for now, skipping encryption since transcripts don't use it either. Every branch syncs since trails carry memories, sync happens per-repo across all branches, and auto-sync should reuse the parent CLI's existing cell resolution and auth rather than env vars — meaning CLI changes are fair game. Statement-level attribution is required so each fact tracks its author, which has implications for the wire protocol.

factmerge.Record needs an additive author field since content-derived IDs shouldn't include it, mirroring how Kind/Locus were handled. Since multiple authors can contribute the same fact, I'm leaning toward per-anchor attribution for provenance plus a record-level created_by field. Data stays region-local with no cross-region replication, matching the existing placement model.

With these decisions made, I should walk through the design in sections per the brainstorming approach — propose, present, get approval section by section — since the user asked to come back with questions or talk through the design together.

A few open questions remain: first, where this new service should live — a new repo or inside an existing monorepo — and which existing internal service (like entiredb or entire-core) is the best template to model after, plus how entire-api handles routing/transport to it. Second, how attribution should tie to identity, likely via Entire account ID.

Since merges happen client-side with CAS pushing whole blobs, the server can't easily know who added which record unless it diffs old vs new heads on advance and stamps attribution in a side table, or we move to a record-level upsert API instead of blob CAS. Given statement-level attribution and the need for searchable per-record data for the memories trail, a relational schema with one row per fact seems like the better fit.

I'm weighing two options: reuse the existing blob-CAS protocol (keeping the ~9.5k lines of tested client code) with the server deriving a row-per-fact projection for search and attribution by diffing heads on advance, versus building a new record-level API where the client pushes deltas directly and the server stores rows natively. I'm leaning toward reusing the blob-CAS approach since it preserves tested client code while letting the server stamp authorship for any record present in the new head but absent from the old one.

Other open questions: how to handle two members adding the same content-ID fact simultaneously (first writer gets attribution, anchors union), whether trail "memories" UI work belongs in this effort or should just expose an API for the web team to consume, and whether retrieval for other developers needs hosted MCP read tools or if pull-down during daemon refresh is sufficient for v1 — I'm leaning toward pull-down only.

For search, I'm thinking server-side lexical search via Postgres FTS is enough for v1, skipping embeddings entirely. On token plumbing, I need to check how the parent CLI injects credentials into the plugin — env vars at spawn time versus a dedicated `entire auth token` helper command — which means digging into the CLI repo's existing credential storage. Deletion is simpler without encryption since it's just row deletion, and region-local storage should satisfy jurisdictional retention requirements.

I also want to reconsider egress gates: auto-sync effectively flips the default posture for connected repos, so I should keep a NO_EGRESS override available. Following the brainstorming approach, I'll present the full design in sections — architecture, data model, API, client changes, trail integration, auth, rollout — along with remaining open questions, rather than pausing after each piece given how the user framed this as a talk-through. Before writing it up, it's probably worth quickly checking the CLI repo for its auth and cell-resolution patterns, plus how entire-api routes to internal services, so the design can concretely reuse that existing logic.

Rather than guess at internal architecture, I should just note this as something to confirm during implementation and move the design forward. I'll frame it as reusing the CLI's existing credential and placement resolution logic, with the exact mechanism to be verified later, rather than stalling the conversation on light digging I can't fully complete right now.

The CLI pushes checkpoints to the hosted API, repos have placements with apiBaseUrl, and get_me confirms a github auth provider — good enough to mark as "confirm during implementation" rather than dig deeper now. I'll also note that the m4-brain prototype branches in entire-api can be mined for schema/tests even though we're building a new service from scratch, without re-litigating that point.

For the architecture, I'm sketching a new internal service (working name entire-brain-api) deployed per cell/region like other internal services, with entire-api routing `/api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/brain/*` to it while applying standard repo authn/authz at the edge.

Now I'm thinking through regionality: data lives in the existing regional Aurora Postgres cluster in new tables owned by this service, but repos can have multiple placements (mirrors across jurisdictions), raising the question of whether facts should exist independently per region or sync to a home region the way checkpoints do via placement apiBaseUrl resolution — leaning toward the simplest option given the "no cross-region" constraint.

I'm settling on facts living in a repo's primary/home region only, with the service itself deployed in every region, flagging the mirror question as a minor open item. For the Aurora data model I'm sketching a `brain_fact_sets` table keyed by repo_id, branch, head_ref, version, and updated_at, using a CAS pattern where head_ref encodes a hash of the blob and advancing the head is an atomic conditional update.

Adding more tables...

Attribution should be server-authoritative: on advance, the server diffs the new head against the old to determine which fact IDs were added or had status transitions, then stamps those with the caller's identity from the token rather than trusting any client-claimed author field. Since merged blobs can carry other members' facts, diffing against the old head isolates exactly what this advance introduced, and attribution per fact can be returned as a sidecar map on GET without restructuring the NDJSON itself.

I'd recommend adding an optional `author` field to factmerge.Record additively, populated from server attribution during pull and kept outside the content-ID hash so it doesn't affect record identity. For the API surface, I need to implement the exact wire format the client already expects to keep things in lockstep, starting with the GET endpoint for branch facts and the POST endpoint for repos.

The advance endpoint should return 412 on CAS conflicts with a changed flag, and I need proposal GET/POST plus resolve endpoints. I'm also adding a new memories read model endpoint for the trail UI and search, consumed by the trail web interface, while hosted MCP support can wait for v2.

On the client side, the CLI needs to inject the resolved placement API base URL, bearer token, and repo ULID into the plugin environment, since those variables are already part of the plugin contract — per-repo connected state will enable auto-sync.

For entire-brain, I'm adding a sync step to the daemon's watch tick after refresh, plus a post-distill hook on session-end, both non-fatal and cursor-throttled, with auto mode gated on the binding existing so it replaces the manual env opt-in once the CLI is connected (NO_EGRESS still takes priority). I also need to close the pull gap by writing the merged head facts back into the local store after sync, modeled on the facts import write path — origin stays put, but I need to figure out how to mark foreign facts, since the merged result includes both local and remote facts that need to be upserted with content-ID dedup, and I want to track which facts came from remote via the shared ledger or binding.

Then I'm planning per-branch sync: syncing the current branch plus the default branch on each tick rather than every branch every tick, and adding an author passthrough for blind-spot notes. For trail memories, the plan is a page that queries the memories read model by repo and branch, showing facts with authors and full-text search, plus a repo-level default-branch view — though who actually builds that UI is still open. For rollout, I'm sequencing it into five phases: service/schema/facts endpoints with pinned compat tests, CLI token injection and auto-sync, pull-into-local with blind-spot handling, the trail memories read model and UI, and finally the proposals surface — with some remaining open questions to sort through.

I'm noting the open questions worth resolving before moving forward: which internal service to model the new one on and where it should live, whether the attribution design (server-stamped authorship, optional additive author field, first-writer-wins) holds up, whether facts should live only in the processing-primary region for multi-region repos, whether the trail memories UI is actually in our scope, and what to cut from v1 — likely skipping hosted MCP read tools and whole-brain artifact publishing.

For encryption, plaintext blobs/rows in Aurora with cluster-level at-rest encryption seems fine and matches how transcripts are handled. Given this is a design walkthrough, I'll aim for moderate detail organized into sections, and rather than pausing after each one per the usual skill flow, I'll present all sections together and invite corrections at the end since that's more practical async. I'll hold off on writing the actual spec doc until I get approval on this design first.

content.text:
All eight answers incorporated. One reconciliation note first, then the revised design.

**On "no server-side code exists":** entire-api (`et/entirehq/entire-api`) does have an unmerged prototype branch train (`m4-brain-1-store` … `m4-brain-9-proposals-api` plus `audit/brain-*`, July–Aug 2026) implementing exactly this path against Postgres. I'm taking your direction — new internal service, built from scratch — but those branches are worth mining for the wire-compat tests (one pins the released entire-brain client's exact request bodies) and for CAS edge cases (ABA, no-op-advance-against-moved-head, branch normalization) even if we don't reuse the code. Also noted: per your answer 3, we drop the prototype's envelope-encryption layer entirely — plaintext rows/blobs in Aurora, same as transcripts, relying on cluster-level at-rest encryption.

# Revised design

## 1. Architecture

A new internal service (working name **brainstore**), deployed per region like the other internal services, fronted by entire-api which routes `/api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/brain/*` to it and enforces the standard repo authz at the edge: read = pull grant, write = push grant. Tables live in the existing regional Aurora cluster. The service is deployed in every region; a given repo's memories live only in that repo's home region (no cross-region replication, per your answer 8).

## 2. Protocol: keep the client's existing wire, add a read model

The released entire-brain client already speaks a complete, tested protocol (read-merge-CAS over a whole-branch NDJSON blob). We implement that server-side verbatim rather than inventing a record-level API:

- `GET /brain/facts?branch=` → `{found, ref, version, data}`
- `POST /brain/facts/advance` → CAS on `(repo, branch)` head; 412 on conflict, `changed:false` on no-op
- `GET/POST /brain/facts/proposals[…/resolve]` → cross-member conflict queue

This reuses ~9.5k lines of tested client code (merge engine, egress scrubbing, identity verification, retry loop) unchanged. The merge stays client-side, so the server stays thin — fitting your routing-service architecture.

## 3. Aurora schema (the part that serves your answers 4 & 7)

Blob-CAS alone can't give you statement-level attribution or a searchable trail section, so the server **derives a row-per-fact projection on every advance**:

- `brain_fact_heads(repo_id, branch, head_ref, version)` — the CAS pointer; advance is `UPDATE … WHERE head_ref = $old`.
- `brain_fact_blobs(repo_id, ref, data)` — content-addressed NDJSON blobs (the protocol's unit).
- `brain_facts(repo_id, branch, fact_id, text, kind, paths, locus, status, superseded_by, created_by_account_id, created_at, last_action_by, updated_at, tsv)` — projection rows with a Postgres FTS column. This is what the trail "memories" section and repo-level views query.
- `brain_fact_events(repo_id, branch, fact_id, account_id, action, at)` — statement-level attribution audit: on each advance the server diffs new head vs old head; facts that appear are `added` by the caller (resolved from the bearer token — server-authoritative, not client-claimed git email), status flips are `superseded`/`retracted`/`revived` by the caller.

Attribution nuance to be aware of: fact IDs are content-derived, so two developers who state the same thing produce the *same* fact — the first to sync it gets `added`; later contributors appear as provenance, not authors. I think that's correct behavior, but calling it out.

The local record format gains one **additive, optional `author` field** (outside the content-ID hash, exactly how `kind`/`locus` were added) so pulled-down facts carry attribution into brief/recall output.

## 4. Upload path (client)

- **cli change (your answer 6):** the parent CLI already resolves placement (`apiBaseUrl` per region) and holds the member token for checkpoint push. It injects `ENTIRE_API_URL` / `ENTIRE_API_TOKEN` / `ENTIRE_REPO_ID` into the plugin environment — which is *already* the plugin's expected contract, so the plugin needs no new config surface. A repo is "connected" when the CLI provides these; that replaces the manual `ENTIRE_BRAIN_ALLOW_HOSTED` env dance. `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS` stays as the absolute kill switch.
- **Triggers:** a `sync` step in the daemon's `watchTick` (after refresh, cursor-throttled) and in `hook session-end` right after distill lands new facts; both non-fatal per the existing NEVER-FAILS rule. Per your answers 4–5: sync is per repo, and syncs the **current branch + default branch** each tick (every branch gets synced as it's worked on, which is what the trail attachment needs, without sweeping all branches every 5 minutes).

## 5. Download path (the known client gap)

After `Sync` returns the merged head, write other members' facts into the local branch store — modelled on `facts import`'s write path (upsert + manifest refresh under the write lock), so remote facts become first-class in brief/recall/query immediately. Plus: a pull-only step in `refresh`/`setup` (so a fresh clone gets the team's memories before ever syncing up), and a new clause in `blind_spot.go` ("N facts exist on the hosted brain for this branch — run sync"). Embeddings for pulled facts are computed locally on first query, exactly like local facts (shipping vectors is useless across embedder models).

## 6. Trail memories section

Trails attach to a change branch; the memories section is a query against the projection: `GET /brain/memories?branch=<trail branch>&q=<search>` returning facts + attribution, FTS-ranked. Repo-level view is the same query on the default branch. entire-api exposes it next to the existing trail sub-resources.

## 7. Build order

1. brainstore service + schema + facts/advance endpoints, with wire-compat tests pinned against the released client's exact bodies (mined from the m4 branches).
2. CLI token/placement injection → plugin auto-sync (daemon + session-end).
3. Pull-into-local-store + blind-spot notice.
4. Memories read model + trail/repo endpoints.
5. Proposals endpoints + settlement (client side already complete).

# Remaining questions

1. **Service template & transport:** which existing internal service should brainstore be modelled on, and how does entire-api call internal services today — internal mTLS HTTP, or proto RPC like the entiredb modules? (Decides scaffolding, and whether this is a new repo or a service in an existing one.)
2. **Projection vs. blob tension:** are you OK keeping the blob-CAS protocol with a server-derived row projection (my recommendation, reuses the client wholesale), or do you want a native row-level API even at the cost of rewriting the client sync? The projection approach means the blob is the source of truth and rows are derived.
3. **Trail UI:** are we building the web UI memories section too, or just the API it consumes?
4. **v1 cut:** facts only — skip the whole-brain artifact publish (`/brain/artifacts`) and the hosted MCP read tools for now? Pull-into-local makes them redundant for the developer loop; the trail section covers the browsing need.
5. **Proposals in v1?** The keep-both merge queues cross-member conflicts as proposals. We can ship v1 where conflicts just coexist cross-linked (both facts stay active) and add the proposal review surface in a fast-follow — or include it from the start. Your call on sequencing.

Answer these and I'll write the spec document and the implementation plan.

# entire-search

A GitHub webhook event processor and search indexing service. It consumes GitHub webhook events from a NATS JetStream queue, processes checkpoint transcripts, commits, and pull requests, generates embeddings via Cohere, and indexes them into Turbopuffer for vector search.

## Architecture

```
GitHub Webhook → webhook-ingest → NATS JetStream → entire-search Consumer
                                                           │
                                                     Handler (routes events)
                                                           │
                                    ┌──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐
                                    │                      │                      │
                             Checkpoint Push         Commit Push           Pull Request
                                    │                      │                      │
                              Hydration + Transcript   DB Lookup          Metadata Extract
                                    │                      │                      │
                                Chunking              Embedding              Embedding
                                    │                      │                      │
                                    └──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┘
                                                           │
                                                    Turbopuffer (vector DB)
```

## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `serve` | Starts the NATS consumer and health check HTTP server |
| `backfill` | Runs historical indexing for a repo (`--repo` or `--repo-name`, `--type commits\|checkpoints\|all`) |
| `backfill --commit-range base..head` / `--ref <ref>` | Indexes only that range (e.g. a `repo_refs_dlq_v1` capture's old_target..new_target) or what a ref adds over the default branch, instead of all of HEAD. Commits only, single `--repo-name`. Targets must be full 40-hex SHAs, `HEAD`, or `refs/` names (EntireDB reads anything else as a branch name); checkpoint and shadow-branch refs are refused. A missing base/head is an error; an empty range is a warning. Replays index a superset of the live event (no first-parent walk) |

## Project Structure

```
cmd/entire-search/       Entry point (serve, query-serve, backfill, patch-repo-id)
internal/
  handler/               Routes webhook events, builds checkpoint/commit/PR docs
  consumer/              NATS JetStream consumer with exponential backoff retry
  transcript/            Fetches transcript JSONL from go-git-api via ConnectRPC
  githubauth/            GitHub App JWT signing, per-installation token minting/caching
  hydration/             Hydration error sentinels shared with the handler (the live poller is a no-op)
  model/                 Repo / checkpoint / commit records shared by the pipeline
  searchapi/             Query API: core-JWT auth and the HTTP search route
  searcher/              Query orchestration: core /repos access resolver, Turbopuffer fan-out, rerank
  entiredb/              EntireDB / entire-core clients and the handler / backfill adapters
  indexer/               Turbopuffer vector DB client, batches embeddings
  embedder/              Cohere API client for text embeddings
  chunker/               Splits transcripts into overlapping chunks
  backfill/              Historical indexing runner
  checkpoint/            Storage version handling and transcript path construction
  strip/                 Text stripping utilities (markdown, code fences, etc.)
  githuberr/             GitHub error classification
  config/                Configuration parsing
  telemetry/             OpenTelemetry traces and metrics
```

## External Services

- **NATS JetStream** - message queue for GitHub webhooks

# Hosted Memory Sync: brain facts → brainstore (Aurora) → teammates

Status: approved design, pre-implementation (2026-10-06). Owner: evis.

Close the loop for durable facts ("memories"): a fact distilled or authored on
one developer's machine uploads to a hosted, region-local store and arrives in
every teammate's local brain, where `brief`/`recall`/`query` serve it like any
local fact. A trail's change branch gets a searchable "memories" read model for
the web UI (UI itself is out of scope here).

## Locked decisions

- **New internal service ("brainstore"), modeled on entire-search.** entire-api
  is a spec-aggregating reverse proxy; brainstore serves its own HTTP API plus a
  static `openapi.yaml` the gateway fetches, merges, and proxies (the
  entire-search pattern: `entire-search/internal/searchapi/server.go`). Caller
  auth is the core JWT the gateway forwards (JWKS-verified; `sub` = account
  ULID). Outbound internal hops use SPIFFE workload mTLS via
  `entiredb/modules/authmtls`. Brainstore is an **optional** upstream (like
  peregrine): its outage degrades only `/brain/*` routes, never cell readiness.
- **Keep the released client's wire protocol unchanged.** The entire-brain
  plugin already ships a complete sync client; v1 hooks it up end to end before
  anything is redesigned. Blob-CAS is the source of truth; rows are derived.
- **Storage: existing regional Aurora cluster, plaintext.** No envelope
  encryption (transcripts are not envelope-encrypted either; cluster-level
  at-rest encryption applies).
- **Scope: per-repo, per-branch.** Facts are keyed `(repo, branch)` — matching
  the local store — because trails attach to branches. Repo-level view = the
  default branch. Project-level later; never org-level.
- **Statement-level attribution, server-stamped.** Who added/retracted each
  fact, resolved from the verified JWT — never from client-claimed identity.
- **Region-local.** Brainstore deploys in every region; a repo's facts live
  only in its home region. No cross-region replication.
- **v1 cuts:** no whole-brain artifact publish (`/brain/artifacts`), no hosted
  MCP read tools, no proposal review/settlement UX. Cross-member conflicts stay
  keep-both (both facts active, cross-linked) until a later phase.

## The loop

```
dev session → distill/remember → facts/<branch>/facts.ndjson      (exists)
  → daemon tick + session-end hook run `facts sync` (http backend) (new trigger wiring)
  → read-merge-CAS against brainstore head                        (client exists; server new)
  → brainstore: blob + CAS head + derived fact rows in Aurora     (new service)
  → teammate's sync/refresh pulls head → merges INTO local store  (new client step)
  → teammate's brief/recall serves it                             (exists, unchanged)
```

## What already exists (client side, do not rebuild)

| Component | Where | Role |

  ULID). Outbound internal hops use SPIFFE workload mTLS via

  peregrine): its outage degrades only `/brain/*` routes, never cell readiness.

## Out of scope / later

Proposal review + settlement UX; whole-brain artifact publish; hosted MCP read
tools; project-level scope; web UI; cross-region anything; vitality/usage
aggregation (stays local per `docs/memory_lifecycle_plan.md`).

## Risks

- **Per-branch head growth:** one head per branch per repo; stale branches
  accumulate. Acceptable for v1 (heads are small); add retention/GC with the
  trail lifecycle later.
- **Whole-set blob transport:** fine at current fact-set sizes (NDJSON, 16 MiB
  line cap); if sets grow large, the row projection already positions a future
  delta API without a storage migration.
- **Attribution first-writer-wins** on identical statements (content-derived
  IDs). Accepted; provenance anchors still record every contributor's sessions.

content.text:
Good question to push on — reading the code closely, my claim was too strong. Here's the full picture:

**What a proposal is.** During sync's keep-both merge, when your local fact and a teammate's hosted fact *conflict* — same taxonomy path, different statements, similarity below the 0.75 auto-merge threshold — the merge refuses to pick a winner. Both facts stay active and cross-linked, and it emits a **proposal**: a record saying "these two should maybe be merged or one should supersede the other," for a human to settle later via `facts review`/`facts proposals`. So proposals are a *byproduct* of syncing, even though nobody reviews them in v1.

**What sync does with them.** After the fact head advances, the sync command (`facts_sync_cmd.go:130-232`) tries to push the local proposal queue to a shared proposal set on the server (so all members see the same conflicts) and reads it back to reconcile — if a teammate settled a conflict, your machine stops re-listing it.

**Where I overstated it.** The client already anticipates a server without proposal endpoints: it returns a typed `ErrProposalQueueUnsupported`, prints a warning ("backend has no shared review queue; N proposal(s) stay in the local queue"), and **the sync still completes** — the code comment literally names "entire-api predating the endpoint" as the expected case. So omitting the endpoints does *not* break sync. The spec's rationale sentence is wrong and I'll fix it.

**The actual v1 choice:**

- **A — ship the proposal store endpoints** (no review UX): ~2 endpoints reusing the exact same blob+CAS storage as facts (the schema already covers it via `kind=proposals`). Conflicts become visible to the whole team via `facts proposals list`, and settlements reconcile across machines when you build the review flow later.
- **B — skip them entirely in v1**: smallest possible server. Cost: every sync that raised conflicts prints the warning, and each developer's conflict queue stays siloed on their machine until the endpoints exist.

My recommendation is still A because the marginal cost over the facts endpoints is genuinely small and B leaves a permanent warning in the loop you're trying to prove — but B is perfectly viable for "end to end working first." Which do you want? I'll correct the spec's rationale line either way.

content.text:
1. **`GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/brain/facts?branch=…`** — returns the branch's current fact-set head: `{found, ref, version, data}`, where `data` is the whole NDJSON fact set (base64) and `ref` is its content hash. The client merges its local facts against this. Pull-gated.

2. **`POST /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/brain/facts/advance`** — body `{branch, oldRef, data}`: stores the client's merged fact set as a new blob and compare-and-swaps the branch head from `oldRef` to it. `412` if the head moved (client re-reads and re-merges), `changed:false` if the merge added nothing. On success the server diffs new vs. old head to write the per-fact rows and attribution events. Push-gated.

3. **`GET /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/brain/memories?branch=…&q=…`** — read model for the trail/repo UI: returns individual fact rows (text, kind, status, author, timestamps) from the derived projection, full-text-searched via `q`. The plugin never calls this; it exists for the web UI you'll build later.

First two are the sync protocol the released client already speaks; the third is new and additive.

content.thinking:
The name "advance" sticks because it matches the pinned wire contract the released client already expects, so renaming it would mean touching a client we agreed not to change. Semantically it's also not a plain create — it's a CAS head-advance moving a pointer from an old ref to a new blob, which "POST /facts" would misleadingly suggest as just adding an individual fact.

The RESTful alternative would be PUT /facts with If-Match: oldRef, which gives 412 semantics natively — but since the client already speaks /advance with an oldRef body, that's the constraint we're working within.

content.text:
Two reasons:

1. **It's the released client's wire contract.** `factsync/httpserver.go:28-34` pins `POST …/brain/facts/advance` with body `{branch, oldRef, data}`. We agreed not to touch the client, so the server serves that path verbatim.

2. **The semantics aren't "create a fact."** `POST /facts` implies appending a resource. This operation is a compare-and-swap on the branch's head pointer: "replace the entire fact set, but only if the head is still `oldRef` — otherwise 412 and I'll re-merge." The verb names the state transition, which is the whole contract (the 412/re-merge loop is what prevents two developers syncing concurrently from losing each other's facts).

The idiomatic REST alternative would be `PUT /facts` with an `If-Match: <ref>` header doing the same CAS — equally correct, but it buys nothing and costs a client change. If we ever redesign the protocol (the "rip things out later" phase), that's the shape I'd pick.

content.text:
# Review PR

Review a pull request with structured, actionable feedback.

## Arguments

- `review the implementation plan and work on getting it tready to start implementing. don't write any code yet, just review the plan` — PR number, URL, or branch name. If empty, review the current branch's open PR.

## Process

### 1. Fetch PR context

```
gh pr view <pr> --json title,body,baseRefName,headRefName,additions,deletions,changedFiles,commits,author
gh pr diff <pr>
```

Read the PR description carefully — it defines scope and intent. Everything you review should be evaluated against what the PR is trying to accomplish.

### 2. Understand the change

Before reviewing line-by-line:
- What is this PR doing and why?
- What files are touched and what's the blast radius?
- Are there any architectural implications?

### 3. Review with this checklist

**Correctness**
- Does the code do what the PR description says?
- Are there logic errors, off-by-one bugs, or unhandled edge cases?
- Are error paths handled correctly?

**Security**
- Any injection risks (SQL, XSS, command injection)?
- Are secrets, tokens, or credentials handled safely?
- Are inputs validated at system boundaries?

**Testing**
- Are there tests for the new/changed behavior?
- Do tests cover edge cases, not just the happy path?
- Are test assertions meaningful (not just "doesn't throw")?

**Design**
- Does the change follow existing codebase patterns and conventions?
- Is the abstraction level appropriate (not over/under-engineered)?
- Are there unnecessary changes outside the stated scope?

**Performance**
- Any N+1 queries, unbounded loops, or missing pagination?
- Are there opportunities for batching or caching that were missed?
- Will this scale with the data sizes it will encounter?

**Readability**
- Are names clear and consistent with the codebase?
- Is complex logic adequately explained?
- Would a future reader understand the "why" behind non-obvious decisions?

### 4. Adversarial review

Take a second, adversarial pass over the diff. Actively try to break the change — assume it has flaws and hunt for them across:

- **Performance** — worst-case inputs, hot paths, allocations, contention.
- **Stability** — race conditions, partial failures, retries, resource leaks, crash recovery.
- **Correctness** — inputs and states that violate the author's assumptions.
- **Simplicity** — code that could be deleted or replaced with something simpler/stdlib.
- **Platform design standards** — deviations from the platform's established design patterns and conventions.

Add any findings to the output using the same severity format.

### 5. Run /simplify

Run the `/simplify` skill (via the Skill tool) against the changed code and fold its findings into the review output.

### 6. Structure your output

For each finding, use this format:

**[severity] file:line — short title**
Description of the issue and why it matters. Include a suggested fix when possible.

Severity levels:
- **[blocking]** — Must fix before merge. Correctness bugs, security issues, data loss risks.
- **[important]** — Should fix. Design problems, missing tests for critical paths, performance issues.
- **[nit]** — Nice to fix. Style, naming, minor improvements. Don't block merge on these.
- **[question]** — Not necessarily wrong, but needs clarification or discussion.

### 7. Summary

End with a brief summary:
- Overall assessment (approve / request changes / needs discussion)
- What the PR does well
- Top 1-3 items that need attention
- Any scope concerns (changes that seem unrelated to the stated goal)

## Guidelines

- Review what's in the diff, not what you wish was there. Don't request unrelated refactoring.
- If the PR is large, focus on the most impactful files first.
- Be specific — "this could be better" is not useful. Show what "better" looks like.
- Distinguish between "this is wrong" and "I would do this differently." Only the former is blocking.
- If you're unsure about something, use [question] severity instead of asserting it's wrong.
- Read relevant source files (not just the diff) when you need context about how changed code integrates with the rest of the system.

- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

All claims verified. One more key discovery while verifying: `entire auth token --jurisdiction <slug>` already exists in the CLI (`cli/cmd/entire/cli/auth.go:141`) and mints exactly the data-plane cell token entire-api cells require — and the help text confirms cells **reject the control-plane bearer**. That resolves one finding and creates another. Here's the review.

Note: there's no PR for this branch (nothing pushed), so the review target is the plan itself — `docs/hosted_memory_sync_plan.md` (the branch's only diff vs main), evaluated for implementation readiness. `/simplify` was skipped: the diff contains no code.

---

## Findings

**[blocking] docs/hosted_memory_sync_plan.md — brainstore cannot import `factmerge` (it's `internal/`)**
The plan requires the server to verify content IDs (`RecordID(text, paths)`) and diff heads into fact rows — both need `factmerge`'s NDJSON parsing, text/path normalization, and ID derivation. That package lives at `internal/factmerge`, which Go forbids importing from another module. It was written dependency-free "explicitly so it is reusable server-side," but it isn't importable today. Options: (a) move it to an exported path in this module (`factmerge/` — mechanical, aliases in `internal/cli` keep the plugin unchanged), (b) a separate tiny module, (c) reimplement the subset in brainstore with golden cross-tests. Recommend (a). **Needs your call before implementation starts.**

**[important] Token acquisition for the daemon was wrong in the plan**
The plan said the CLI injects `ENTIRE_API_TOKEN` into the plugin env. That works for session-end hooks (CLI is in the exec chain) but not the daemon: the launchd plist env is baked once at install (`setup_daemon.go:97-101`), and these are expiring JWTs — a baked token is both a secret-on-disk and stale within hours. Fix: the plugin mints a fresh token per sync by shelling out to `entire auth token --jurisdiction <slug>` (PATH is already in the plist env; the plugin already shells out to `entire`). Only the non-secrets (base URL, repo ULID, jurisdiction) get persisted — the per-branch `hosted-target.json` binding already stores two of them. This also shrinks the Phase-3 CLI change considerably. *Applied to the doc below.*

**[important] Wrong token class would fail auth silently late**
Phase-2 manual testing and brainstore's verifier must use the **jurisdictional** token (`--jurisdiction us`), not the control-plane bearer — cells reject the latter. Brainstore copies entire-search's JWKS verifier/issuer config. *Applied.*

**[important] Advance semantics were under-specified — the prototype had bugs in exactly these spots**
Three contract points the plan must pin (the audit commits in entire-api fixed each after the fact): (1) create case — empty `oldRef` means create-if-absent; empty/stale `oldRef` against an existing head is 412, never an overwrite; (2) the no-op answer (`changed:false`) is only valid when the head still equals `oldRef` — a no-op against a moved head is 412, or the client loses the lost-update signal; (3) the request body carries BOTH `oldRef` and `old_ref` — a framework that rejects undeclared fields (huma's `additionalProperties:false`) 422s every released client unless both are declared. Verified response decode fields: `found/ref/version/data` and `newRef/version/changed`; `data` is base64 both directions. *Applied.*

**[important] Missing input caps**
Client enforces a branch-length cap (`ErrBranchTooLong`) and a 16 MiB NDJSON line cap; the server must mirror a branch cap, trim the branch key (one branch = one head), validate the repo-id path segment, and cap the advance body. *Applied.*

**[nit] Memories search**
Use `websearch_to_tsquery`/`plainto_tsquery` for `q` (never raw tsquery composition) and paginate. *Applied.*

**[question] Attribution edge**
Advance-diff attributes every fact new-to-the-head to the syncing member — including facts they merely carried (e.g., merged locally days earlier). In practice facts originate where they sync from, so this is mostly right, but a second clone or a backfill import can attribute someone else's statements to the uploader. Accept for v1?

**[question] Where does brainstore live?**
New repo (`entirehq/brainstore`-ish) vs. a new service directory inside an existing repo. Affects CI/deploy scaffolding — needed before Phase 1.

## Summary

**Assessment: ready to implement once two decisions land.** The plan's core is sound — it reuses a tested client protocol verbatim, the server stays thin, and every wire claim now traces to a specific line in the released client. The findings above are committed into the doc (f203526d); the fixed-up plan is at [docs/hosted_memory_sync_plan.md](/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/baghdad/docs/hosted_memory_sync_plan.md).

What blocks starting:

1. **`internal/factmerge` export** — brainstore needs its ID derivation/NDJSON parsing and can't import an `internal/` package across modules. My recommendation: move it to `factmerge/` in this repo (mechanical, plugin unchanged via aliases). Your call.
2. **Where brainstore lives** — new repo vs. directory in an existing one. Needed for Phase-1 scaffolding.

And one accept/reject: **attribution is "who synced it first,"** which can misattribute carried facts (second clone, imports). Fine for v1 in my view since facts originate where they sync from, but it's a product behavior you should consciously accept.

What the plan does well: zero client protocol changes (the whole loop is provable end-to-end before any redesign), the token story now has no persisted secrets, and each prototype bug from the abandoned entire-api branches is pinned as an explicit server obligation with a test requirement.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/evisdrenova/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.4.1/skills/writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter

# Factmerge Export Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Move `internal/factmerge` to the exported path `factmerge/` so the new brainstore service (a separate Go module) can import the fact content-ID derivation, normalization, and NDJSON codec.

**Architecture:** Pure mechanical package move inside the `github.com/entireio/entire-brain` module — no API, behavior, or test changes. `factmerge` is already dependency-free pure Go (no filesystem, no cgo) by design; exporting it is a path change plus an import-path rewrite in the 31 files that import it. `internal/cli`'s alias file (`facts_aliases.go`) keeps every CLI type name unchanged.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27, gofmt via `mise run fmt`, `go test -race`.

**Spec:** `docs/hosted_memory_sync_plan.md` (section "Brainstore (new service)", prerequisite paragraph).

## Global Constraints

- Module path stays `github.com/entireio/entire-brain`; new package path is `github.com/entireio/entire-brain/factmerge`.
- No exported-identifier renames, no behavior changes, no test edits beyond import paths — the diff must be reviewable as a pure move.
- This package becomes public API of the module: from this commit on, changes to its exported surface follow the same additive-only discipline the wire contract documents (`docs/brain_wire_contract.md`, versioning rules).
- Formatter is `gofmt` (`mise run fmt`); tests run with `-race` (`mise run test:ci`).

## Review Focus

1. A stale import of `internal/factmerge` left anywhere (including testdata-referencing helpers or build-tagged files `grep` might miss on a casual pass) — the build catches untagged files, so the pinning test is the full `go build ./...` over all build tags in use; step 3 greps with `-r --include="*.go"` across the whole tree to cover tagged files too.
2. `package factmerge` doc comment still says it lives under `internal/` or claims server-side reuse is future work — misleads the brainstore implementer; step 2 updates the doc comment.
3. `testdata/` paths inside the package are relative; the move must carry the directory wholesale (`git mv` of the parent dir does) or the NDJSON fuzz/boundary tests fail on missing fixtures — covered by running the package tests in step 4.
4. Another checkout/branch importing `internal/factmerge` merges after this lands and breaks — unavoidable repo-wide rename cost; the commit message names the old→new path so the fix is a sed, and the move is a single atomic commit (no window where both paths exist).
5. Accidental export of a second internal package via transitive references — `factmerge` imports nothing from this repo (verify in step 1), so none exists.

---

### Task 1: Move `internal/factmerge` to `factmerge/` and rewrite imports

**Files:**
- Move: `internal/factmerge/` → `factmerge/` (whole directory incl. `testdata/`)
- Modify: the 31 importers (10 in `internal/cli`, 19 in `internal/factsync`, 2 in `internal/hostedbrain`, 1 in `internal/factgitmeta` — exact list via the grep in step 3)
- Test: existing suites only (`factmerge` has 8 test files; importers' suites prove the rewrite)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing new.
- Produces: `github.com/entireio/entire-brain/factmerge` with the existing exported surface unchanged — `Record`, `Anchor`, `Proposal`, `RecordID(text string, paths []string) string`, `NormalizeText`, `NormalizePaths`, `VerifyIdentity`/`VerifyIdentities`, `Upsert`, `UnionAnchors`, `ApplyActions`, `Promote`, `Retract`, `GC`, `ParseNDJSON`, `WriteNDJSON`, `MaxPaths`, `MaxLineBytes`, `DefaultConfidenceThreshold`. Brainstore's plan imports exactly these.

- [ ] **Step 1: Confirm the package is self-contained (no same-repo imports)**

Run:
```bash
grep -rn "entireio/entire-brain" internal/factmerge/*.go | grep -v "_test.go" | grep import -A0 || true
grep -rn "\"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/" internal/factmerge/ || echo "self-contained"
```
Expected: `self-contained` (the package imports only stdlib). If anything prints, STOP — the move would drag another internal package public; report instead of proceeding.

- [ ] **Step 2: Move the directory and fix the package doc comment**

Run:
```bash
git mv internal/factmerge factmerge
```
Then open `factmerge/merge.go` (or wherever the `// Package factmerge …` doc comment lives — find it with `grep -l "^// Package factmerge" factmerge/*.go`) and, only if it references `internal/` placement or describes server-side reuse as hypothetical, update it to state the current fact, e.g.:

```go
// Package factmerge is the deterministic fact-set merge core shared by the
// entire-brain CLI and the hosted brainstore service: content-derived record
// identity, normalization, keep-both promotion, and the NDJSON codec. It is
// deliberately pure Go with no filesystem, agent, or cgo dependencies so both
// sides of the sync wire run the identical merge semantics.
```

Do not change any identifier.

- [ ] **Step 3: Rewrite the import path in every importer**

Run:
```bash
grep -rl --include="*.go" "entire-brain/internal/factmerge" . \
  | xargs sed -i '' 's#entire-brain/internal/factmerge#entire-brain/factmerge#g'
grep -rn --include="*.go" "internal/factmerge" . && echo "STALE IMPORTS REMAIN" || echo "clean"
```
Expected: `clean`.

- [ ] **Step 4: Format, build, and run the full suite with race detection**

Run:
```bash
mise run fmt
go build ./...
mise run test:ci
```
Expected: no diff from fmt beyond the edited files; build and all tests PASS. The `factmerge` suite (ndjson fuzz/boundary/size/utf8, identity, merge, dedup, proposal validation) proves fixtures moved intact; `internal/cli` + `internal/factsync` suites prove the rewrite.

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit (explicit paths, no `git add -A`)**

```bash
git add factmerge internal/cli internal/factsync internal/hostedbrain internal/factgitmeta
git status --short   # verify ONLY the move + import rewrites are staged; stage any missed importer explicitly
git commit -m "refactor: export factmerge for the brainstore service

Move internal/factmerge to factmerge/ (github.com/entireio/entire-brain/factmerge)
so the hosted brainstore service can import the content-ID derivation,
normalization, and NDJSON codec. Pure move: no exported identifier or
behavior changes; importers' paths rewritten (internal/factmerge -> factmerge).

Per docs/hosted_memory_sync_plan.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27, gofmt via `mise run fmt`, `go test -race`.

**Spec:** `docs/hosted_memory_sync_plan.md` (section "Brainstore (new service)", prerequisite paragraph).

## Global Constraints

- Module path stays `github.com/entireio/entire-brain`; new package path is `github.com/entireio/entire-brain/factmerge`.
- No exported-identifier renames, no behavior changes, no test edits beyond import paths — the diff must be reviewable as a pure move.
- This package becomes public API of the module: from this commit on, changes to its exported surface follow the same additive-only discipline the wire contract documents (`docs/brain_wire_contract.md`, versioning rules).
- Formatter is `gofmt` (`mise run fmt`); tests run with `-race` (`mise run test:ci`).

## Review Focus

1. A stale import of `internal/factmerge` left anywhere (including testdata-referencing helpers or build-tagged files `grep` might miss on a casual pass) — the build catches untagged files, so the pinning test is the full `go build ./...` over all build tags in use; step 3 greps with `-r --include="*.go"` across the whole tree to cover tagged files too.
2. `package factmerge` doc comment still says it lives under `internal/` or claims server-side reuse is future work — misleads the brainstore implementer; step 2 updates the doc comment.
3. `testdata/` paths inside the package are relative; the move must carry the directory wholesale (`git mv` of the parent dir does) or the NDJSON fuzz/boundary tests fail on missing fixtures — covered by running the package tests in step 4.
4. Another checkout/branch importing `internal/factmerge` merges after this lands and breaks — unavoidable repo-wide rename cost; the commit message names the old→new path so the fix is a sed, and the move is a single atomic commit (no window where both paths exist).
5. Accidental export of a second internal package via transitive references — `factmerge` imports nothing from this repo (verify in step 1), so none exists.

---

### Task 1: Move `internal/factmerge` to `factmerge/` and rewrite imports

**Files:**
- Move: `internal/factmerge/` → `factmerge/` (whole directory incl. `testdata/`)
- Modify: the 31 importers (10 in `internal/cli`, 19 in `internal/factsync`, 2 in `internal/hostedbrain`, 1 in `internal/factgitmeta` — exact list via the grep in step 3)
- Test: existing suites only (`factmerge` has 8 test files; importers' suites prove the rewrite)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing new.
- Produces: `github.com/entireio/entire-brain/factmerge` with the existing exported surface unchanged — `Record`, `Anchor`, `Proposal`, `RecordID(text string, paths []string) string`, `NormalizeText`, `NormalizePaths`, `VerifyIdentity`/`VerifyIdentities`, `Upsert`, `UnionAnchors`, `ApplyActions`, `Promote`, `Retract`, `GC`, `ParseNDJSON`, `WriteNDJSON`, `MaxPaths`, `MaxLineBytes`, `DefaultConfidenceThreshold`. Brainstore's plan imports exactly these.

- [ ] **Step 1: Confirm the package is self-contained (no same-repo imports)**

Run:
```bash
grep -rn "entireio/entire-brain" internal/factmerge/*.go | grep -v "_test.go" | grep import -A0 || true
grep -rn "\"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/" internal/factmerge/ || echo "self-contained"
```
Expected: `self-contained` (the package imports only stdlib). If anything prints, STOP — the move would drag another internal package public; report instead of proceeding.

- [ ] **Step 2: Move the directory and fix the package doc comment**

Run:
```bash
git mv internal/factmerge factmerge
```
Then open `factmerge/merge.go` (or wherever the `// Package factmerge …` doc comment lives — find it with `grep -l "^// Package factmerge" factmerge/*.go`) and, only if it references `internal/` placement or describes server-side reuse as hypothetical, update it to state the current fact, e.g.:

// identity, normalization, keep-both promotion, and the NDJSON codec. It is
// deliberately pure Go with no filesystem, agent, or cgo dependencies so both

```

Do not change any identifier.

- [ ] **Step 3: Rewrite the import path in every importer**

Run:
```bash

grep -rn --include="*.go" "internal/factmerge" . && echo "STALE IMPORTS REMAIN" || echo "clean"
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Format, build, and run the full suite with race detection**

go build ./...
mise run test:ci

Per docs/hosted_memory_sync_plan.md.
